full_caption: Kingsmere Homeowners Association, Inc., Appellant, v. Deepwell Realty Trust, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Kingsmere Homeowners Association, Inc. appeals the denial by the Ashbourne County Board of Adjustment of a use variance permitting operation of a transit maintenance yard at 2625 Tanner's Row, Ashbourne, NR, a parcel zoned R-1A single-family residential.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The parcel is 920 square feet, irregular in shape, and burdened by a drainage easement across 5 percent of its buildable area. Those are conditions of the land and not of the owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: An area variance is governed by a balancing test weighing the benefit to the applicant against the detriment to the health, safety and welfare of the neighborhood, and does not require the showing of hardship applicable to use variances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Spot zoning is the singling out of a small parcel for treatment differing from that of surrounding property, for the benefit of the owner and to the detriment of the comprehensive plan. The rezoning here served a plan objective and is not spot zoning.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Exhaustion of administrative remedies is a prerequisite to judicial review. A facial constitutional challenge to the ordinance is excepted from that requirement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: A nonconforming use lawfully existing at the effective date of the ordinance may continue but may not be enlarged, and is lost by abandonment or by discontinuance for the period specified in the ordinance.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Discontinuance for 18 months is presumed abandonment under Section 18.1 of the ordinance. The presumption is rebutted by proof of an intent to resume coupled with overt acts consistent with that intent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Vested rights against a subsequent ordinance arise where the developer, in good-faith reliance on a validly issued permit, has made substantial expenditures. Kingsmere Homeowners Association, Inc. expended $125,000 on site work before the moratorium was adopted.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Hardship must arise from the land itself and not from the owner's personal circumstances or from a self-created condition. Purchase with knowledge of the restriction is a factor but is not, standing alone, disqualifying.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The denial is vacated and the matter remanded to the Board for findings addressing the drainage easement and the shape of the parcel.

sections.heading: RIDER C — NONCONFORMING USE AND ABANDONMENT
sections.text: A use lawfully existing on the effective date of this ordinance may continue in its then-existing scope but shall not be enlarged, extended to additional land, or changed to another nonconforming use. Discontinuance of the use for 18 consecutive months creates a rebuttable presumption of abandonment, which may be overcome by evidence of an intent to resume together with overt acts consistent with that intent.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 7 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Severability
sections.text: If any provision of this instrument is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to render it enforceable, and if it cannot be so reformed it shall be severed, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Waiver and Course of Dealing
sections.text: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party charged. The acceptance of a payment with knowledge of a breach, the failure to insist on strict performance, or any course of dealing between the parties shall not constitute a waiver of that or any subsequent breach, nor estop the party from enforcing the provision thereafter.
